classification.difficultyReason: Translate each side-length triple into a right triangle without a supplied diagram, identify the hypotenuse, choose a ratio for one acute angle and use the complementary-angle relationship to obtain all three angles.

content.prompt: What are the sizes of the angles, correct to the nearest degree, in a:

answer.worked:
The hypotenuse has length $5$. Let $\alpha$ be opposite the side of length $3$, and let $\beta$ be the other acute angle.
$$\begin{align*}\sin\alpha&=\frac35\\\alpha&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac35\right)\\\alpha&\approx37^{\circ}\\\beta&=90^{\circ}-\sin^{-1}\left(\frac35\right)\\\beta&\approx53^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
The angles are $37^{\circ},\ 53^{\circ}$ and $90^{\circ}$.

The hypotenuse has length $13$. Let $\alpha$ be opposite the side of length $5$, and let $\beta$ be the other acute angle.
$$\begin{align*}\sin\alpha&=\frac5{13}\\\alpha&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac5{13}\right)\\\alpha&\approx23^{\circ}\\\beta&=90^{\circ}-\sin^{-1}\left(\frac5{13}\right)\\\beta&\approx67^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
The angles are $23^{\circ},\ 67^{\circ}$ and $90^{\circ}$.

The hypotenuse has length $25$. Let $\alpha$ be opposite the side of length $7$, and let $\beta$ be the other acute angle.
$$\begin{align*}\sin\alpha&=\frac7{25}\\\alpha&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac7{25}\right)\\\alpha&\approx16^{\circ}\\\beta&=90^{\circ}-\sin^{-1}\left(\frac7{25}\right)\\\beta&\approx74^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
The angles are $16^{\circ},\ 74^{\circ}$ and $90^{\circ}$.
